title: Polite Email Requests to Foreign Dealers: Can, Could & Please
description: Compose polite, clear email requests to international truck distributors regarding order confirmations and vehicle specs.
learning_objectives: Use polite request modals: Could you please, Can you send
Structure polite professional opening and closing phrases
Avoid overly blunt imperative commands in customer communications

questions.prompt: Dear Mr. Schmidt, _____ you please send us the updated chassis delivery address?

explanations.correct: Polite email request formula takes 'Could you please + base verb': 'Could you please send'.
explanations.wrong_D: 'Do' is not a polite request modal here.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'Mohl byste nám prosím poslat...?'. Standard polite business inquiry: 'Could you please send us...'.

questions.prompt: Please _____ the attached proforma invoice for the five military chassis units.

explanations.correct: Polite request with 'Please' takes base verb form: 'Please find'.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'V příloze naleznete...'. Standard formula: 'Please find the attached invoice'.

questions.prompt: Could you confirm if the customer _____ right-hand drive or left-hand drive cabs?
questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'Zda zákazník požaduje...'. Singular customer takes '-s': 'requires'.

questions.prompt: We _____ forward the full technical datasheet by 15:00 today.

explanations.correct: Capability/willingness modal takes bare verb: 'can forward'.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'Můžeme přeposlat...'. Modal 'can' takes bare base verb without 'to': 'can forward'.

questions.prompt: Please let me know if you _____ any further assistance with the tender documentation.
questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'pokud potřebujete jakoukoliv pomoc'. Standard email formula: 'if you need any assistance'.

questions.prompt: _____ you like us to schedule a Teams video call with our chief suspension engineer?

explanations.correct: Polite offer formula is 'Would you like [someone] to [verb]'.
explanations.wrong_A: 'Do you like' asks about general preference, not an offer.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'Přáli byste si, abychom naplánovali...?'. Polite offer takes 'Would you like us to schedule...'.

questions.prompt: I look forward to _____ from you regarding the dealer agreement contract.

explanations.correct: Prepositional idiom 'look forward to' must be followed by gerund (-ing): 'to hearing'.
explanations.wrong_A: 'hear' is a frequent Czenglish error following 'to'.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'Těším se na vaši zprávu'. 'Look forward to' is a preposition $\rightarrow$ requires '-ing': 'look forward to hearing from you'.

questions.prompt: Could you please inform us when the bank transfer _____ completed?

explanations.correct: Passive construction for completed state takes 'is completed'.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'kdy bude převod dokončen'. Use 'when the transfer is completed'.

questions.prompt: We are pleased to _____ you that the first three prototype trucks are ready for inspection.

explanations.correct: Formal business email formula: 'We are pleased to inform you that...'.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'S potěšením vám oznamujeme'. Standard formula: 'pleased to inform you'.

questions.prompt: Thank you for your inquiry; we will reply _____ your technical questions by Friday.

explanations.correct: Verb 'reply' pairs strictly with preposition 'to': 'reply to your questions'.
explanations.wrong_C: 'reply on' is a literal Czenglish error (*odpovědět na*).

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'odpovědět na dotazy'. Never say *reply on*. Always use 'reply TO your questions'.
